generator.params.dioecious.why: A dioecious species' plants are male or female: a male plant flowers but bears no fruit or seed cones, a female one bears them. Where both sexes sit on every plant, every plant fruits.

generator.params.space_kill.why: Corner's rules: the smaller its leaves, the slenderer a plant's twigs and the more they branch. A shoot grows no nearer the plant than this, so the twigs filling a crown sit as far apart as the cube root of the area of the leaf card a short shoot bears (one leaf, or a sprig of small ones), and a crown of small leaves branches as finely as its leaves are small.

generator.params.space_density.why: One point of free space for each cube the shoot spacing spans, so the spacing, not a lack of free space, decides how finely the crown branches.

generator.params.adult_age.why: A plant flowers, or bears cones, from the end of its juvenile period.

generator.params.unit_nodes.rule: max(1, min(round(shoot_leaves / (leaves_per_node * max_shoot)), floor(4 * internode * (leaves_per_node < 2 ? 2 : 1) / leaf_size)))
generator.params.unit_nodes.why: A year's shoot is a growth unit of many short internodes, not a few long ones: a vigorous shoot, as long as the program's most internodes a bud grows in a year, bears the taxon's leaves per vigorous long shoot, so each of its internodes is divided into as many nodes as that takes, but never into nodes nearer than a quarter of a leaf's length, so a large-leaved plant's shoots carry fewer; on a spiral, where each leaf turns from the one below it and the next on its side stands two nodes up, never nearer than an eighth.

generator.params.long_share.why: Only some of a growth unit's buds grow into long shoots, the rest into short shoots: the few nearest its tip on an acrotonic shoot or its foot on a basitonic one, more of them reaching down its middle on a mesotonic one.

generator.params.short_share.why: Next to the buds that may grow long shoots, a third as many grow short shoots; the growth unit's other buds stay latent.

generator.params.bud_base.why: A basitonic shoot grows its long shoots from the buds nearest its foot, so the plant renews itself from below; the others from those nearest its tip.

generator.params.dormant_buds.why: Where a taxon's old limbs and trunk sprout, buds that did not grow stay dormant under the bark and grow a new shoot where light comes back to them (delayed reiteration).

generator.params.shed_ratio.why: A plant that sheds its own shaded limbs drops a limb whose leaves gather less light than its wood costs: under a twentieth of a fully lit leaf per segment it carries. Where no source says whether it self-prunes, a shade-intolerant tree is taken to: its shaded limbs die, as black cottonwood's do, which stands on a trunk clear of branches for more than half its length (FEIS).

generator.params.space_renew.why: Where a shed limb leaves a gap, the crown can grow back into it.

generator.params.bole_clear.why: A tree that sheds its own shaded limbs stands on a clear trunk below its crown, and so, where no source says, does a shade-intolerant one.

generator.params.limb_arch.why: Limbs rise from the stem and turn outward as they lengthen: a little in a vase, more in a dome, most where a crown spreads wider than tall, and most of all under an umbrella.

generator.params.crown_ratio.why: A conifer that sheds its own shaded limbs keeps living branches only on the upper part of its height, so it stands on a clear bole.

generator.params.apex_whorl.why: Where branches are built like the trunk (Rauh's and Attims' models, as in pines), a branch apex spreads a small whorl of its own each year; where they are flat (Massart's and Roux's, as in firs), it forks to each side.

generator.params.flat_top.why: Every axis of an umbrella crown, the stem's too, levels out near the top, so the crown spreads flat; a flat-topped head levels out only in its top tenth.

generator.params.crown_widest.why: A dome is widest at its middle, a spreading crown a little above it, a vase and an umbrella near the top, and a cone in its bottom third, as the Urban Tree Database classes a paraboloid crown (McPherson et al. 2016, GTR-253, crown shape 3: widest in the bottom third; 0.17, that third's middle).

generator.params.crown_fullness.why: An umbrella's region fills out toward a flat-ended drum.

generator.params.room_height.why: An umbrella stops at its flat top, and a cone at its leader's tip: its free space reaches no higher than the crown, so a cone's widest part stands low where its own height puts it, not part way up a region taller than the tree.

generator.params.terminal_bloom.why: A shoot whose tip ends in flowers grows on from the buds below them, so an adult crown forks where it flowers: most often where flowers only end shoots.

generator.params.tip_bloom.why: Where flowers end the shoots, a shoot that has stopped growing at the crown's edge still ends each year in them, so they stand on the crown's surface, not inside it.

generator.params.bloom_pairs.why: A shoot that ends in its flowers unfolds its year's leaves below them: as many pairs as the taxon's flowering shoot bears leaves, two to a pair (or two single leaves on a spiral).

generator.params.bloom_years.why: Where flowers come on new shoots, a shoot that has ended in its cluster flowers no more and next year's come on the shoots beyond it, so a short shoot or a stopped tip flowers in its first year only; spurs flower year after year.

generator.params.apex_death.why: A sympodial axis is carried on by a lateral when its tip dies or stops, so where a shoot's tip has no free space left it may die and leave the buds below it to fork.

generator.params.tip_abort.why: Where a shoot has no true terminal bud its tip dies at the end of every season and the topmost lateral bud carries it on, turned toward its own side, sometimes with the next bud down beside it: its twigs zigzag and its limbs wander and fork, where a terminal bud's run straight on.

generator.params.plagio.why: Where a plant's side shoots lie flat, every shoot a limb bears holds itself near level and sets its buds and leaves to either side, so the limb carries level sprays.

generator.params.set_point.why: A limb's reaction wood holds it at the angle from upright its taxon's floras describe: near upright when erect, a third of the way to level when ascending, past half way when spreading, level when horizontal.

generator.params.fork_set.why: Where a tree's leader is lost, the stems its trunk divides into lean out as scaffold limbs, at somewhat less than its limbs' own angle, instead of each rising as a leader; its head is broad and round, not a cluster of spires.

generator.params.crown_units.why: Where a tree's leader is lost and its trunk divides into scaffold limbs, each limb builds a crown of its own (sequential reiteration, Barthélémy and Caraglio 2007), so the crown is as many domes as limbs, not one smooth dome. An umbrella's or a flat-topped head's limbs level out into one flat top (Troll's model) instead.

generator.params.limb_turn.why: A tortuous limb turns its own way from year to year, each year's shoot setting off at a chance angle that its held angle only partly takes back, so the wood runs in long irregular curves.

generator.params.branch_droop.why: Branches and branchlets that droop or hang bend toward the ground more than the limbs that carry them, which reaction wood holds up.

generator.params.branch_hold.why: A drooping or pendulous branch does not hold its angle against its own weight as a limb does, so it arches over and its ends hang.

rules.generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): the sexual system its taxa state most often decides; a species whose taxa state dioecy no more often than another system bears both sexes on every plant until it states its own.

rules.generator.params.space_kill.note: Corner's rules of axial conformity and ramification (Corner 1949), measured across species by Westoby and Wright (2003, Oecologia 135: 621-628): thicker twigs bear larger leaves and branch less. The spacing goes as the cube root of the short shoot's leaf card's area, so that crowns hold about as much leaf per volume whatever the card's size; its constant, 2, is fitted to the Urban Tree Database's desert genera (usfs-urban-tree-database-2016: Chilopsis, Parkinsonia, Prosopis and Vachellia farnesiana, irrigated city trees) by leaf area per crown area.

rules.generator.params.space_density.note: A choice of the model's: free space sampled as finely as shoots may be spaced (space colonization, Runions, Lane and Prusinkiewicz 2007).

rules.generator.params.adult_age.note: The juvenile period is the time from germination to the first flowers, cones or seed, which the Woody Plant Seed Manual's tables give as the minimum seed-bearing age (spec rework P6). adult_age is the first year a program measuring it by the plant's age lets the plant flower or bear cones, so it is the juvenile period itself.

rules.generator.params.unit_nodes.note: Critchfield (1971, read in full) found a maple's long shoot about as long as its leaf pairs are many, each pair a few centimetres up the stem; so a shoot of the program's longest year's growth carries the taxon's shoot_leaves, and each of the program's internodes is cut into as many nodes as that takes. The internode the program grows by is a step of vigour, not a node. Corner's rules (Corner 1949) tie a twig's leaves to its spacing: the larger the leaves, the fewer and farther apart, so nodes are kept at least a quarter of the leaf card's length apart. That spacing is between leaves that stand over one another: a pair's over the pair below it, but a spiral's single leaf (137.5° round from the one below) over none nearer than two nodes up, so alternate leaves may stand an eighth of the card apart (shrub habit, 2026-10-18), as a sumac's 30 cm to 50 cm leaves crowd a few centimetres apart at its stout twigs' tips (FEIS, Rhus glabra: branches sparse and stout).

rules.generator.params.long_share.note: Barthélémy and Caraglio (2007, read in excerpts): the buds that grow are concentrated toward one end of the annual shoot (acrotony, basitony) or in its middle (mesotony). How many is the model's choice: as many as the steps of vigour the shoot grew, so a shoot keeps the buds able to grow long that it had before it was cut into a growth unit, gathered at its tip or its foot, or twice as many reaching into its middle; the rest grow short shoots.

rules.generator.params.bud_base.note: Barthélémy and Caraglio (2007, read in excerpts): a basitonic shoot branches mostly from its proximal part.

rules.generator.params.dormant_buds.note: Meier, Saunders and Michler (2012, read in full): epicormic shoots grow from buds that stay dormant on the stem, single or in clusters, released when the light or the tree's state changes. The program keeps one dormant bud a node where the taxon is epicormic.

rules.generator.params.shed_ratio.note: A choice of the model's, after the self-organizing tree models of Pałubicki and others (2009), whose shedding rule was not read here: a limb is shed when the light its tips gather falls below a twentieth of a segment's worth for each segment it carries. The value is the maple program's, which grew bigleaf maple to the Urban Tree Database's crowns.

rules.generator.params.space_renew.note: A choice of the model's: where a self-pruning plant sheds a limb, the space the limb held frees again, as old trees rebuild their crowns from sprouts.

rules.generator.params.bole_clear.note: A choice of the model's (broadleaf revision 16): branches below the crown's base are shed as it rises, never at or above where the stem forks. Checked against iNaturalist photographs of open-grown Garry oak, whose crowns stand on a few metres of clear trunk.

rules.generator.params.crown_ratio.note: A choice of the model's (pinidae revision 10): a self-pruning conifer keeps living branches on the top 0.6 of its height. Fitted by eye to iNaturalist photographs of ponderosa pine; FEIS notes that some open-grown trees keep branches nearly to the ground, so it is a middling value, not a forest one.

rules.generator.params.apex_whorl.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) pp. 484-485 (Hallé, Oldeman and Tomlinson's models): in Rauh's model, and Attims' (its continuous form), the branches are built like the trunk; in Massart's, and Roux's, they are horizontal, by symmetry. The count, three side shoots a year, is a choice of the model's (pinidae revision 10), fitted by eye to iNaturalist photographs of ponderosa pine.

rules.generator.params.limb_arch.note: A choice of the model's (broadleaf revision 16): degrees a limb's held angle grows per metre of limb wood. Fitted by eye to iNaturalist photographs of open-grown Garry oak (spreading) and umbrella thorn (umbrella), not measured.

rules.generator.params.flat_top.note: A choice of the model's (broadleaf revision 16), with flat_topped (growth-form language, 2026-10-19: at 0.9 sassafras's head levels off flat, as Sargent's 'narrow usually flat-topped head', with its height within 6%), after Troll's model in Halle, Oldeman and Tomlinson's architectural models, whose axes are all plagiotropic: shoots level out above three quarters of the crown's height. Fitted by eye to iNaturalist photographs of umbrella thorn.

rules.generator.params.crown_widest.note: A choice of the model's (broadleaf revision 16): where each crown form's region is widest, by eye from photographs of open-grown trees; conical (2026-10-24) from the Urban Tree Database's paraboloid crown class (McPherson, van Doorn and Peper 2016, PSW-GTR-253, crown shape 3, widest in the bottom third), at that third's middle.

rules.generator.params.crown_fullness.note: A choice of the model's (broadleaf revision 16): an umbrella's region fills toward a drum, by eye from photographs of umbrella thorn.

rules.generator.params.room_height.note: A choice of the model's (broadleaf revision 16): an umbrella's free space stops at its crown's height, so nothing grows above the flat top; a cone's too (2026-10-24), so southern magnolia's widest part stands near the ground as in its photographs, not at its top.

rules.generator.params.terminal_bloom.note: A choice of the model's: a shoot that ends in flowers is carried on by the buds below them, so the crown forks; the chance a year, 0.35, is the maple program's, fitted to bigleaf maple, and half that where flowers may also sit beside the leaves.

rules.generator.params.bloom_pairs.note: A choice of the model's (broadleaf revision 22): the program unfolds a short shoot's leaves in pairs (two single leaves on a spiral), so a flowering shoot's stated leaves become half as many pairs, at least one.

rules.generator.params.bloom_years.note: A choice of the model's (broadleaf revision 22): an inflorescence that ends a shoot ends that axis, so it flowers once; the model's short shoots and stopped tips stand for those flowering shoots and flower only in their first year where the taxon flowers on new shoots.

rules.generator.params.tip_bloom.note: A choice of the model's (broadleaf revision 17): a lineage whose flowers end its shoots bears them at the tips that have stopped at the crown's edge, as well as where a growing shoot ends in flowers (terminal_bloom).

rules.generator.params.apex_death.note: A choice of the model's: a sympodial axis is carried on by a lateral when its tip stops, so a tip with no free space left aborts with the maple program's chance, 0.1 a year.

rules.generator.params.tip_abort.note: Hallé, Oldeman and Tomlinson (1978): a sympodial axis is built of modules, each ending when its apex dies or stops and continued by a lateral. The winter keys state it as a genus character: Sargent's Manual (sargent-1922, analytical key to the genera, pp. xxiii-xxiv) divides the genera with 'Terminal buds wanting; branchlets prolonged by an upper axillary bud' (Morus, Tilia, Ulmus, Celtis, Ceanothus, Carpinus, Ostrya, Betula) from those with terminal buds present. That the tip dies every year (1) is that statement; the turn of the bud that takes over (abort_angle 25) and the share of years two buds take over together (abort_fork 0.3) are the model's choices (branching form, 2026-10-19), against open-grown photos in which Betula, Alnus and Corylus twigs zigzag and leaders are lost or multiple (inaturalist-photos-2026-10, imagekit runs branching-chat-woody-forms-2026-10-19).

rules.generator.params.plagio.note: Hallé, Oldeman and Tomlinson (1978): orthotropic axes grow upright with their leaves and buds all round them, plagiotropic ones near horizontal with leaves and buds in one plane, and a tree's architecture is told largely by which of its axes are which (Troll's, Roux's and Massart's models among them). Drawing every shoot a limb bears as flat (plagio_set 80 from upright, buds and leaves to either side in turn) while the limb's own axis rises and arches is the model's choice (branching form, 2026-10-19).

rules.generator.params.set_point.note: Sargent's Manual words each tree's limbs by their angle ('erect branches', Populus trichocarpa p. 126; 'stout ascending or spreading branches', Quercus garryana p. 296; 'short stout ... branches spreading almost at right angles', Sassafras p. 363). The degrees for each word are the model's choice (growth-form language, 2026-10-19): Garry oak at 35 rises in a vase and sassafras at 80 holds its limbs out level, as written, where every tree held 50 before.

rules.generator.params.fork_set.note: Sargent describes trunks that divide into a few large limbs under broad heads ('usually divided near the ground into several large diverging stems ... forming a broad round-topped head', Umbellularia p. 361; tanoak 'in open positions spreading horizontally and forming a broad dense symmetrical round-topped crown', p. 237). Holding two divided stems at 0.6 of the limbs' angle, and more stems closer together in proportion (1.2 of it over their number), is the model's choice (growth-form language trial, 2026-10-19): tanoak's two stems at 40 degrees grow its broad round crown with its leaf area kept, where held upright they grew two spires and where apical control was relaxed instead the tree starved (16 m to 10 m); California bay's three stems at 36 degrees left a notch between three points where Sargent's head is round-topped, and at 24 they close into one round head.

rules.generator.params.crown_units.note: Barthélémy and Caraglio (2007, Reiteration, read 2026-10-25 at PubMed Central PMC2802949): 'automatic' or 'sequential' reiteration is 'a very common and major morphogenetic process underlying crown construction in most forest trees'; the young tree builds its architectural unit and then repeats it, so the mature crown is a set of reiterated complexes, each built like the whole plant (their Fig. 27). One sub-crown for each stem a lost leader's trunk divides into (fork_stems) is the model's reading of it; each a copy of the crown's region shrunk to an equal share of its area and moved out until it meets the region's edge, so the crown keeps its measured width, is the model's choice (sub-crowns trial, 2026-10-25): bigleaf maple then grows a broad lobed dome on a short branching bole, as Silvics describes and its open-grown photos show, and Oregon white oak a lumpy dome (outline fit 0.75 against photos' 0.75 to 0.85, where one region grew 0.92). An umbrella's flat top is left as one region: sub-crowns rounded an umbrella thorn's top.

rules.generator.params.limb_turn.note: Sargent calls some trees' limbs 'contorted' (Populus tremuloides p. 121; Sassafras p. 363) or 'crooked' (Prosopis juliflora var. velutina p. 602); Imagekit's woody-forms photo tallies (2026-10-19) find madrone's limbs wavy in 25 of 28 votes (tortuous in 9 of 23) and red-osier dogwood's straight in 48 of 49. A year's turn of 25 degrees spread kinks sassafras's and madrone's limbs visibly with their heights within 7% (growth-form language trial, 2026-10-19); flexuous is about half of it.

rules.generator.params.branch_hold.note: Sargent's 'slender pendulous branches' (Salix Scouleriana p. 161) and 'somewhat pendulous toward the ends' (Populus tremuloides p. 121) describe branches that arch over and hang at their ends. With branches held back toward the limbs' angle at the plant's incline rate of 0.3 a node, no droop bent a Scouler willow's short shoots; at 0.05 they arch over and hang, with its height within 9% of its reference (growth-form language trial, 2026-10-19). Drooping is between the two.

rules.generator.params.branch_droop.note: Sargent describes limbs and branchlets apart, often with opposite habits: 'stout often pendulous branches' (Acer macrophyllum p. 688), 'slender somewhat pendulous branches' (Alnus rubra p. 223), 'horizontal and often pendulous on older trees' (Betula p. 205). A branch droop of 0.12 hangs a paper birch's branchlets at its crown's edge with its limbs held as before and its height within 1% (growth-form language trial, 2026-10-19); drooping is half of it.

rules.generator.params.short_share.note: Barthélémy and Caraglio (2007, read in excerpts) describe the buds of a growth unit grading along it, the most vigorous laterals at its favoured end; the buds farthest from it often never grow. How many grow short shoots is the model's choice: a third as many as may grow long ones, fitted so open-grown crowns hold the leaf area per crown area of the Urban Tree Database's trees (as many as the long ones gave an 80-year Oregon white oak 6.4 m² a m² against valley oaks' 1.9 to 5.3; none halved red alder's leaf area).

generator.defaults.note: Where a species states no size for a forb's leaf length, the median of the built-in forbs' own values (2026-10-14). The rules of the flowering plants' form, nearer, set it from the species' facts; these yield to a lineage program's values and any file's.

Where a species states no size for a graminoid's blade and culm, the median of the built-in graminoids' own values (2026-10-14). The rules of the flowering plants' form, nearer, set it from the species' facts; these yield to a lineage program's values and any file's.

Where a species states no size for a vine's leaf card, the median of the built-in vines' own values (2026-10-14). The rules of the flowering plants' form, nearer, set it from the species' facts; these yield to a lineage program's values and any file's.

Where a species states no stem diameter or flower size for a stem succulent, the medians of the built-in columnar stem succulents' values (2026-10-14). The rules of the flowering plants' form, nearer, set it from the species' facts; these yield to a lineage program's values and any file's.

Where a species states no leaf length, height or flower size for a rosette succulent, the medians of the built-in rosette succulents' values (2026-10-14). The rules of the flowering plants' form, nearer, set it from the species' facts; these yield to a lineage program's values and any file's.
